# Polish pass

## Images inspected
All six: visual-evidence/{desktop,mobile}-{catalog,booking,requests}.png.

## Findings
- Catalog (desktop and mobile): the BMW card shows a broken or not-yet-loaded image. The native alt text "Image unavailable" sits at the top-left and overlaps the "Available" badge, and the media box is shorter than on the other cards. This is the only material defect.
- Booking and requests screens: hierarchy, price breakdown, the primary "Request booking" action, status badges, filter pills and mobile nav wrap are legible and show no overflow. No edits were needed.

## Fix
- src/styles/app.css: the card media box now clips overflow. The image and fallback are centered, muted, and sized to fill the 16:10 box. The fallback no longer applies its own aspect ratio, so card heights stay consistent. This is a CSS-only change.

## Checks run
- `npm run build` passed.
- I did not run unit or Playwright checks, and did not regenerate screenshots.

## Limitations
- I have not read any after-change image, so the fix is unverified visually. The runner regenerates evidence.
- If the BMW image URL is genuinely broken, the seed data or server owns that. I could not tell from the screenshot whether it was a failed load or a capture taken mid-load.
- No final visual approval is claimed.

I made one CSS fix for a broken-image problem on the catalog cards. I haven't confirmed it visually, because I didn't regenerate the screenshots or read any after-change image.

I read all six screenshots (desktop and mobile for catalog, booking and requests). The BMW card in the catalog showed the browser's plain "Image unavailable" text at the top-left, overlapping the "Available" badge. Its image box was also shorter than the other two cards. The booking and requests screens looked fine, so I left them alone.

The fix is in `src/styles/app.css`. The card image box now clips overflow, and the placeholder fills the box with centered, muted text. The placeholder no longer sets its own aspect ratio, so card heights should stay consistent.

`npm run build` passed. I didn't run the unit tests or Playwright checks.

I couldn't tell from the screenshot whether the BMW image URL is genuinely broken or the screenshot was taken while it was still loading. If the URL is broken, that is in the seed data or server, which I'm not allowed to edit.

I wrote `quality/polish.md` and made no claim of final visual approval.
